# Skeleton

A placeholder in the shape of content that is about to load, so the layout does not jump when it arrives.

```tsx
import { Skeleton } from "@rata/react";
```

| | |
|---|---|
| Registry name | `skeleton` |
| Family | loading |
| Tier | free |
| Status (css / react / figma) | latest / latest / future |
| Depends on | — |

## Behavior

An `aria-hidden` block. The region that is loading — not the skeleton — carries `aria-busy` and says what is loading. No primitive: it holds no state and takes no input.

- **Skeleton when the layout is known; Spinner when it is not** — A skeleton promises a shape: a list of three rows, a card with a picture. When the shape is known it prevents the layout shift that makes a reader lose their place, and it lets them start reading the page's structure before the data arrives. When the shape is not known — an action in progress, a result of unknown size — a skeleton guesses, and the content that replaces it jumps anyway. That is Spinner's case. A button that is working is always a Spinner, via Button's `loading`.
- **Every skeleton is `aria-hidden`, and the loading region owns the announcement** — A page of twelve skeleton rows that each said "loading" would read the word twelve times. The container whose content is loading sets `aria-busy="true"` and holds one visually-hidden status — or a Spinner with a `label` — naming what is loading; when the content arrives, `aria-busy` comes off and the content is read normally. The skeleton itself is decoration with a layout job, and nothing more.
- **A pulse between two background tokens, not a shimmer gradient** — A gradient sweep needs a highlight colour that exists nowhere in the token set and would have to be invented and contrast-checked per brand; a pulse between `theme.bg.muted` and `theme.bg.subtle` uses two documented steps and changes with the theme for free. It runs at the slow band's slowest step because a skeleton is on screen for a while, and anything faster becomes a flicker in peripheral vision. Under reduced motion it stops entirely: a still block communicates "not yet" perfectly well.
- **Sizing is the caller's, by design** — A skeleton is only useful if it matches the content it stands in for, and only the caller knows that content. `text` sizes itself from the type scale, so a text skeleton is right by construction; `block` and `circle` take the size of whatever they replace — an Avatar's size, a media slot's aspect ratio — from the caller's layout. A `width` and `height` prop would invite exactly the bare pixel values this system has none of.
- **Web and native** — Web: a `span` (so it can sit inside text or inline layout) with `aria-hidden="true"`; the loading container carries `aria-busy`. React Native: a `View` with `importantForAccessibility="no-hide-descendants"` and `accessibilityElementsHidden`, animated with the core `Animated` API and skipped when `AccessibilityInfo.isReduceMotionEnabled()` is true. The container's loading state is `accessibilityState={{ busy: true }}`. All props work on both. Rata-drawn (decision N5): there is no OS placeholder control. The native implementation ships in the pro tier (decision N6).

## Props

Extends `Omit<HTMLAttributes<HTMLSpanElement>, "children" | "aria-hidden">`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| `shape?` | `SkeletonShape` | `"text"` | What kind of content it stands in for. |
| `lines?` | `number` | `1` | How many lines a `text` skeleton stands in for. |
| `className?` | `string` | — | Extra classes, for the size of a `block` or `circle` and its placement. |

### `shape`

```ts
shape?: SkeletonShape = "text"
```

What kind of content it stands in for.

**Use when**

- `text` for lines of running text — sized from the type scale.
- `block` for an image, a chart or a media slot.
- `circle` for an avatar.

**Don't use for**

- `block` for a paragraph. A grey rectangle where text will be does not tell the reader it is text, and it will not match the paragraph's height.

**Accessibility** Visual only. Every shape is `aria-hidden`.

### `lines`

```ts
lines?: number = 1
```

How many lines a `text` skeleton stands in for.

**Use when**

- The usual line count of what replaces it — 3 for a summary, 1 for a title.

**Don't use for**

- Passing it with `block` or `circle`. Only text has lines.

### `className`

```ts
className?: string
```

Extra classes, for the size of a `block` or `circle` and its placement.

**Use when**

- Taking the size of the thing it replaces, from the same layout rule that sizes that thing.

**Don't use for**

- A bare pixel width. Size it from the same token or layout rule as the content it replaces, or the content will jump.

## Use cases

### A list whose shape is known

Rows of a known structure are loading, and the page should not jump when they arrive.

```tsx
<section aria-busy={loading} aria-labelledby="activity-heading">
  <Heading level={2} id="activity-heading">Activity</Heading>
  {loading ? (
    <>
      <Spinner label="Loading activity" />
      <Skeleton lines={2} />
      <Skeleton lines={2} />
    </>
  ) : (
    <ActivityList items={items} />
  )}
</section>
```

The section carries `aria-busy` and the Spinner's `label` is the one announcement; the skeletons are `aria-hidden`, so the word is not read once per row.

### Reaching for the wrong component

A Save button waiting on the server.

```tsx
<Skeleton shape="block" className="button-sized" />
```

Don't. The control already exists and its shape is not in question — that is `<Button loading>`, which keeps the button focusable and announced while it works.

## Real usage in this repo

```tsx
<Skeleton lines={2} />
```

## Token recipe

### base

A recessed block — the use `theme.bg.muted` documents for a skeleton — that pulses gently toward the next background step. No gradient sweep: a pulse needs only two existing tokens and degrades to a still block.

| Property | Token |
|---|---|
| background | `theme.bg.muted` |
| pulse to | `theme.bg.subtle` |
| pulse duration | `motion.duration.slow-max, alternating, with motion.easing.standard` |
| under prefers-reduced-motion | `no animation — a still theme.bg.muted block` |

### text

One bar per line, sized from the type it stands in for so the paragraph that replaces it takes the same space.

| Property | Token |
|---|---|
| block-size | `type.body.size, centred in a line box of type.body.line-height` |
| border-radius | `radius.inner` |
| gap between lines | `none — the line box already carries the leading` |
| last line inline-size | `a shorter fraction of the full width, so the block reads as a paragraph and not a wall` |

### block

A rectangle standing in for an image, a chart or a card's media.

| Property | Token |
|---|---|
| border-radius | `radius.element` |

### circle

A circle standing in for an avatar.

| Property | Token |
|---|---|
| border-radius | `radius.pill` |
